stem: How can a clinician distinguish a septal hematoma from an inferior turbinate during an examination?

options.text: By checking if it mists a mirror
By observing if it is located on the lateral wall versus the medial septum
By the color of the mass
By whether the patient has a fever

explanation: Hematomas arise from the medial septum, while turbinates are structures on the lateral wall of the nose.
rationale: Focus on the physical location where the mass attaches within the nostril.

optionExplanations.A: A mirror test checks for airflow but doesn't identify the anatomical origin of a visible mass.
optionExplanations.B: Hematomas arise from the medial septum, while turbinates are structures on the lateral wall of the nose.
optionExplanations.C: While color can vary, the anatomical attachment point is the most reliable way to differentiate the two.
optionExplanations.D: Fever may occur with a late-stage abscess but does not help differentiate the initial anatomy of the mass.

source.hint: Focus on the physical location where the mass attaches within the nostril.
